claims.text: NbMoTaWVCr powder can be prepared with oxygen content below 0.02 at.%.
NbMoTaWVCr tends to form brittle Laves and oxide phases and to suffer interstitial embrittlement.
SLM at a linear energy density of at least 2.83 J/mm promotes formation of a single BCC solid solution in NbMoTaWVCr.
The high cooling rate of SLM suppresses coarse brittle phases and favors a supersaturated BCC solid solution.
HPT or equivalent severe plastic deformation can refine the NbMoTaWVCr grain size below 500 nm.
Processing under vacuum or argon minimizes oxygen and nitrogen uptake.
Post-deformation annealing below the solvus will stabilize precipitates while preventing grain coarsening.
The proposed SLM-HPT route will produce a BCC matrix with grains below 500 nm and fine, coherent Laves and oxide precipitates.
The desired Laves/oxide precipitate volume fraction is approximately 7–10%.
The relevant secondary phases in NbMoTaWVCr are a (Cr,V)2(Ta,Nb) Laves phase and Ta2VO6 oxide.
Low-oxygen feedstock and rapid solidification reduce detrimental oxygen and nitrogen concentrations in the final alloy.
HPT-generated grain boundaries impede dislocation motion through Hall–Petch strengthening.
The increased grain-boundary density acts as a sink for interstitial impurities and thereby mitigates interstitial brittleness.
Fine Laves and oxide precipitates harden the alloy, pin dislocations, and improve high-temperature stability.
SLM followed by HPT will produce room-temperature yield strength above 3400 MPa and plasticity above 5%.
The resulting alloy will resist creep and oxidation at high temperature because of its stable nanostructure and formation of a protective oxide film.
Conventional cast NbMoTaWVCr generally has coarse grains, more than 10% brittle Laves/oxide phases, ductility below 2%, and poor high-temperature performance.
The strategy may fail for alloys with substantially higher Al or Si because they form brittle silicide or B2 phases.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires HPT to obtain sub-500-nm grains and enhanced strength, but the first falsification condition says that observing no such refinement or strength increase in samples without HPT would falsify the hypothesis. That result would instead be consistent with the proposed need for HPT.

The proposed route mitigates brittleness by maintaining low interstitial content and removing interstitials to grain-boundary sinks, whereas the second falsification condition requires intentionally high-interstitial samples to improve relative to low-interstitial controls. Failure of high-interstitial material to outperform the low-interstitial control would not falsify the stated low-interstitial mechanism.
